headline: Swings to a quarterly loss on FX reversal as revenue slides
summary_short: Liberty Global's Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 7.7% y/y to $1,172.0 million and Adjusted EBITDA slipped 3.1% to $324.9 million, while a reversal in FX and equity-affiliate results pushed the quarter to a $365.1 million net loss from Q1's $337.8 million profit.
summary_long: Consolidated revenue fell 7.7% y/y (organic -6.0%) to $1,172.0M, led by Telenet's residential ARPU declines and subscriber losses plus lower low-margin construction revenue passed through the VMO2 and VodafoneZiggo JVs. Adjusted EBITDA fell 3.1% y/y to $324.9M; operating income collapsed to $3.0M from $29.6M on higher impairment/restructuring charges. Q1's $337.8M shareholder net income swung to a $365.1M net loss on a $122.6M FX translation loss on intercompany balances (versus a Q1 gain) and a $289.9M share of VMO2/VodafoneZiggo JV net losses, both largely non-cash. No 2026 buybacks (unauthorized); cash rose to $2,418.6M on $677.8M EdgeConneX sale proceeds, long-term debt fell to $8,321.7M. No forward guidance was given.

The resolver's raw ebit_usd_m/ebitda_usd_m fields were deliberately NOT used as KPI rows: they are Yahoo's mechanical EBITDA/EBIT (net income plus back out interest/tax/D&A only), which still absorbs the large swings in FX-translation, derivative, and equity-JV losses/gains sitting below operating income, and would misstate the operating trend if shown alongside operating income. The filing's own 'Adjusted EBITDA' ($324.9M) is used instead. drivers.explanation: Telenet revenue fell 4.1% (organic -1.0%) on residential fixed ARPU declines and customer losses, plus lower low-margin nexfibre construction revenue and disposition impacts group-wide.
VMO2 JV EBITDA fell on lower service revenue and a Q1 legal provision; VodafoneZiggo JV EBITDA fell on higher network-resilience, programming and marketing costs, partly offset by cost control.
Impairment, restructuring and other operating items rose to $15.5M in Q2 (from $5.5M a year ago), mostly Telenet restructuring plus acquisition/disposition costs.
The swing from Q1 profit to a net loss reflects a $122.6M intercompany FX translation loss (a Q1 gain reversed) and a $289.9M share of VMO2/VodafoneZiggo JV net losses, both largely non-cash.
No 2026 share buybacks — the board has not authorized a repurchase program; cash rose on $677.8M EdgeConneX sale proceeds and long-term debt was reduced.
